commitResults.messageBody: Move command input, welcome and goodbye screens, separators, indentation, task rendering, and task-count messaging into a dedicated Ui class. Keep Herta focused on command dispatch and task behavior while preserving the existing console contract, including EOF handling.

Move task-file loading, strict UTF-8 reading, storage parsing, serialization validation, and atomic saves out of Herta into a dedicated Storage class. Delegate startup loading and all persisted task mutations through one Storage instance while preserving existing command behavior and error messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract user command parsing into Parser
commitResults.messageBody: Move command recognition, task construction, date and time validation, query arguments, sort validation, and task-number parsing into Parser. Rename Storage.parseTask to parseStoredTask to distinguish serialized-data parsing from user-command parsing, while preserving all existing UI behavior and error messages.

Introduce TaskList as the owner of task storage, indexed lookup, add/remove operations, completion-state updates, rollback support, matching, and stable sorted indices. Update Herta and Storage to exchange TaskList instead of raw mutable lists while preserving task numbering, persistence behavior, and console output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract exit handling into command hierarchy
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce the abstract Command contract with execute and isExit operations, then implement ExitCommand for the bye flow. Extend Parser with an incremental command-object parsing seam and update Herta to execute migrated commands while retaining legacy dispatch for the remaining command types. Preserve all existing console behavior and error handling so the stretch-goal refactor can proceed safely in small steps.

Move task-list display behavior from Herta into a concrete ListCommand that follows the shared Command execution contract. Extend Parser.parse to create ListCommand instances while preserving legacy dispatch for commands that have not yet migrated. Keep list output, task ordering, and persistence behavior unchanged so the command hierarchy can continue to grow incrementally.

Introduce AddCommand as the shared base for commands that append tasks, including persistence-before-mutation and confirmation output. Implement TodoCommand and extend Parser.parse to construct it from validated todo input, removing todo handling from Herta's legacy switch. Preserve existing validation, storage error handling, and console output while preparing deadline and event commands to reuse the same add workflow.

Implement DeadlineCommand as an AddCommand specialization so deadline tasks use the shared persistence, task-list update, and confirmation workflow. Extend Parser.parse to construct DeadlineCommand instances from validated deadline input and remove deadline handling from Herta's legacy switch. Preserve all existing date validation, storage behavior, and console output while continuing the incremental command migration.

Implement EventCommand as the final AddCommand specialization so todo, deadline, and event additions share one execution path for persistence, task-list updates, and confirmation output. Extend Parser.parse to construct EventCommand instances from validated event input and remove the obsolete add helper and event branch from Herta. Preserve event date validation, range checks, storage behavior, and all existing console output.

Introduce TaskIndexCommand to centralize validation of selected task indices and implement DeleteCommand for persistent task removal. Extend Parser.parse to construct DeleteCommand instances from validated delete input, and remove deletion behavior from Herta's legacy switch and helper. Preserve one-based task handling, invalid-input messages, persistence ordering, task numbering, and console output.

Move completion-status mutations, persistence rollback, and user feedback out of Herta and into dedicated MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand classes. Extend Parser command construction for both commands while reusing TaskIndexCommand validation, leaving the interactive behavior unchanged.

Move filtering, upcoming-task lookup, and chronological sorting out of Herta into FilterCommand, UpcomingCommand, and SortCommand. Add QueryCommand to share result rendering for predicate-based queries, and update Parser to construct the new command objects while preserving validation and user-visible output.

Add UnknownCommand so blank and unrecognised inputs are represented in the command hierarchy. Change Parser.parse to return a concrete Command for every input and remove Optional-based fallback dispatch from Herta while preserving all existing error messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor Herta into an application object
commitResults.messageBody: Move Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList into Herta fields, load tasks through the constructor, and expose a run method for the command loop. Keep main as a thin launcher and preserve startup errors, EOF handling, separators, and exit behavior while aligning the entry point with the target OOP design.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions to document important assumptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Add assertions at key domain and command boundaries to verify that:

- task indices remain valid when accessing task lists
- task status changes and rollback preserve the original state
- staged and live task lists remain consistent after updates
- parsed tasks and date/time ranges satisfy established invariants

These checks expose programmer errors during development and document
contracts between components, reducing the risk of inconsistent state.

The save method combines task validation, serialization, filesystem preparation, atomic replacement, and temporary-file cleanup. Its length makes the persistence workflow harder to read and obscures the boundaries between validation and file operations.

Extract those responsibilities into focused private methods and keep save as a short orchestration method. Preserve validation order, user-facing error messages, atomic-move fallback, and cleanup behavior so the refactoring improves readability without changing persistence semantics.

The parseStoredTask method combines storage-line normalization, schema validation, task construction, and completion-state restoration. Its length and mixed abstraction levels make the persistence format harder to understand and make parsing failures harder to localize.

Separate those phases into focused private methods and name the storage indexes and record sizes explicitly. Preserve the existing task formats, validation order, exception messages, and completion-state behavior so this remains a readability-only refactoring.

The parseEvent method combines event-format validation, date parsing, and event construction. Its mixed abstraction levels make the command flow harder to read, while repeated format and date error messages make future edits prone to inconsistency.

Separate input extraction and validation from event construction, and centralize the repeated messages as named constants. Preserve the existing validation order, exception messages, accepted syntax, and event-range behavior so this remains a readability-only refactoring.

The load method handles file validation, record parsing, blank-line
skipping, and line-numbered error translation in one block. These mixed
abstraction levels make the normal path harder to follow and keep the
parsing loop nested inside exception handling.

Extract storage-line iteration and line-specific error translation into
focused helpers. Keep file validation, blank-line handling, task order,
and existing error messages unchanged so the refactoring improves
readability without changing loading behavior.

The run method handles startup, loading failures, command processing,
and shutdown in one block. Mixing these abstraction levels makes the
normal command loop harder to follow and obscures the application's
main flow.

Extract command-loop processing into a focused private helper. Keep
prompts, separators, EOF handling, loading-error behavior, and scanner
shutdown unchanged so the refactoring improves readability without
changing the user-visible behavior.

The event parser returns three related values as a raw String array. Its
caller must remember the positional contract, so a small parsing change
can silently associate the description or a date with the wrong field.
The array also makes the event construction flow harder to read because
the indexes carry no domain meaning.

Replace the array with a private EventParts record whose named accessors
describe each validated value. Preserve all parsing, validation, error
messages, and public APIs while making event construction
self-documenting.

ResponseCategory now identifies exit responses, so Command.isExit is not
read by application code and duplicates that responsibility. Remove the
dead method, its override, and obsolete tests to keep one exit path.

List, query, and sort commands all format numbered tasks the same way,
Duplicate presentation logic risks inconsistent output. Centralize task
rendering in UiOutput so commands only select tasks. This keeps console
and GUI output consistent and preserves existing behavior.

parseUserDate uses an index-based loop only to rethrow a final formatter
failure, which obscures the two supported date formats and leaves an
unreachable configuration error. Express the ISO-then-slash fallback
directly so the control flow is clear while preserving parsing and error
behavior.

The JavaFX entry points use numeric literals for the minimum window size
and exit delay, so their intent is not visible at the call sites. Name
these values to make the UI configuration self-explanatory and easier to
adjust without changing behavior.

The command loop stores an exit flag even though each exit path can

finish the method directly. This makes control flow harder to follow and

keeps the normal command path nested.

Return immediately for EOF and bye responses, then display the separator

for continuing commands. This keeps exit handling at the point it is

detected without changing console behavior.

The constructor initializes the loading error before the try block even

though the success path never changes it. That data flow makes the

initialization less direct for readers.

Assign the loading error in the same branch as the task list result, then

copy both branch results into the final fields. This keeps each value's

origin explicit without changing loading or error behavior.

The console UI and response collector duplicate the same task, numbered

task, and task-count formatting. Keeping both copies risks inconsistent output

when one renderer changes.

Provide these shared operations as UiOutput defaults so each renderer only

defines its message sink and its renderer-specific goodbye behavior. This

reduces duplication without changing the visible output.

MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand duplicate validation, mutation, persistence,

and rollback logic. The duplicated workflow can drift and makes each command

harder to scan.

Extract the transactional status update into TaskStatusCommand, leaving the

concrete commands to provide their distinct messages. This reduces duplication

while preserving rollback behavior when saving fails.

Launcher.main is a public entry-point operation without documentation for

readers who need to understand how the JavaFX application starts.

Add concise Javadoc describing the launch operation and its forwarded

arguments, bringing the class in line with the project's documentation

standard without changing runtime behavior.

The CLI and GUI entry points construct Herta with the same data-file path,
but keeping the path and default construction in separate places allows them
to drift.

Name the default path and route both entry points through Herta's default
constructor. This keeps configuration in one place while preserving the
explicit-path constructor used by tests and alternate deployments.

Storage parsing, reconstruction, and validation repeat task-type and
completion codes as raw literals, including the invalid-status message. Their
meaning is hidden and future format changes can become inconsistent.

Name the protocol values and use them throughout the loading path. This makes
the storage contract explicit while preserving serialized data and error text.

Response styling handles errors outside the category mapping and uses a
nullable style class with a silent default. That can hide unsupported
categories and makes the mapping harder to audit.

Map every response category in one switch, including errors, and fail
explicitly for an unsupported category. This keeps the existing styles while
making future mapping omissions visible to maintainers.

CommandType stores the recognized keyword, but Parser repeats the same
command names when extracting arguments and task indices. These copies can
become inconsistent with command recognition.

Reuse CommandType keywords through one argument-extraction helper and the
existing task-index parser. This keeps recognition and parsing aligned while
preserving the parser API and user-facing behavior.

TaskList has one status-update workflow for mark and unmark operations and a
second branch for restoring a previous status. Separate implementations can
diverge as status handling evolves.

Share one private helper across marking, unmarking, and restoration. This
reduces duplication while retaining public APIs, return values, and rollback
behavior.

Task serialization returns bare numeric completion values, so the meaning
of each branch is implicit and must be inferred from the storage format.

Name the complete and incomplete status codes and use those names in the
serialization helper. This makes the status contract visible without
changing the persisted representation.

The storage writer retries a non-atomic move for every IOException from the
atomic move. That can mask unrelated permission or I/O failures and does not
match the reason given by the fallback comment.

Retry only for unsupported atomic moves or an existing-target conflict, while
letting other I/O errors propagate to the existing save error handling. This
keeps the portability fallback without hiding genuine failures.

Storage.load checks directories separately before checking for a regular
file, and both branches raise the same error. The duplicated guard obscures
the single rule for acceptable data paths.

Rely on the regular-file check for all existing invalid path types while
retaining the missing-file fresh-start behavior. This shortens the happy path
without changing load results or error messages.

The upcoming-days parser uses a deliberately thrown NumberFormatException to route non-positive values through the same handler as nonnumeric input.

Parse the integer first and validate positivity afterward. This keeps exceptions for actual conversion failures, makes the normal path explicit, and preserves the existing user-facing error for invalid ranges.

The parser repeats delimiter literals such as /by, /from, /to, and /on while validating command text. Deadline format errors are also duplicated in two branches.

Name the grammar markers and the shared deadline-format message, then reuse them throughout the parser. This makes the command grammar easier to change consistently while preserving all accepted input and user-facing errors.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name task storage and display type labels
commitResults.messageBody:
Task serializers and display methods repeat task-type codes as raw literals.
These values describe the same task-type contract, but their meaning is not
visible at each use.

Name each task type's storage code and reuse it in both serialization and
display formatting. This keeps the two representations consistent without
changing persisted or user-visible output.

Task completion display relies on raw X and blank-space literals. The method therefore hides the meaning of the two possible status representations behind punctuation.

Name the completed and incomplete status icons and use those names in the status decision. This clarifies the display contract while preserving the existing task output.

The storage preparation guard checks whether the data path is a directory and then checks the broader condition that covers every existing non-regular path. The first check is redundant.

Keep one guard for an existing path that is not a regular file. This states the replacement invariant directly while preserving the existing save and error behavior.

ResponseCategory includes ERROR but its class comment describes only successful responses. DialogBox.applyResponseStyle also describes unsupported categories as a no-op even though unsupported enum values are rejected.

Update both comments to document the actual response and null-category behavior. Accurate contracts help readers understand the error path without changing runtime behavior.

SortCommand uses LocalDateTime.MAX directly as the fallback for tasks without a scheduled time. The sentinel's ordering purpose is implicit in the comparator.

Name the fallback value and document that it places unscheduled tasks after dated tasks. This makes the sorting rule readable without changing task ordering.

Herta.run nests the normal command loop in a conditional and duplicates the scanner cleanup across loading-error and normal exits.

Use a guard clause for loading failures and close the UI in one finally block. This keeps the successful path prominent, centralizes cleanup, and preserves the normal user-visible behavior.

FindCommand passes a bare false to control whether an empty query prints its
heading. The call site does not explain what the flag means.

Expose the behavior through a named QueryCommand helper and keep the boolean
inside the private implementation. Keep overloaded methods adjacent for
Checkstyle compliance. This makes query output policy explicit without
changing displayed results.

Parser already receives the recognized command type, so repeating each enum constant at its dispatch branch duplicates the source of the keyword. Reuse the parsed value when extracting task indices to keep dispatch and argument parsing aligned and make future keyword changes less error-prone.

Main and MainWindow load the same avatar asset but each repeats its resource path. Define the path once with the window's shared UI resources so the application icon and avatar remain aligned and future resource changes have one source of truth.

HertaResponse exposes a two-argument constructor that has no callers in
the application or tests. Remove the dead constructor to keep the public
API focused on the response form used by the GUI and avoid maintaining an
unused compatibility path.

The Javadocs use British spellings in two source files, which is
inconsistent with the project's American English coding standard.
Replace those spellings so documentation remains consistent and easier
to scan.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams for task and command lookup
commitResults.messageBody:
The task list and command parser use explicit loops for collection
lookups.

- Use IntStream pipelines for matching and sorting task indices.
- Use a short-circuiting stream for command recognition.

These transformations preserve existing ordering, matching, and fallback
behavior while making the collection processing more declarative.
